subject: Marketplace listing: tax forms, VAT handling, and invoice split for co-sell deals

Subject: Question on invoicing & tax forms for AWS co-sell listing

Hi Dylan / Vanessa,

We're getting ready to finalize the purchase order for Redwood through the AWS co-sell listing. Our procurement asked whether Redwood or AWS will send the invoice for runtime usage and how VAT / withholding will be handled. Specifics they asked for:
- Do you require a completed W-9 or W-8BEN-E for marketplace buys?
- If we buy via AWS Marketplace (co-sell), will GreenWave receive an invoice from AWS or from Redwood?
- Any extra steps for EU VAT (reverse charge) or Brazil withholding?

We can share our billing contact and W-9 if needed. Please advise — procurement is on a short timeline.

Thanks,
Clara Hayes
Billing Manager, GreenWave Analytics

Hi Clara — thanks for the note and the PO. Quick summary up front: it depends on the exact offer type and whether you accept a SaaS contract via AWS or a private offer. High-level guidance below, followed by next steps we can take to make this procurement straightforward.

- Marketplace vs Vendor invoice: For standard AWS Marketplace listings, AWS invoices the customer for the usage and remits to Redwood; in that flow AWS is the billing entity and will issue the invoice to GreenWave. For private offers or when Redwood is transacting outside the marketplace (direct contract), Redwood invoices directly.

- Tax forms (W-9 / W-8): AWS typically requires the buyer's tax form on file. Redwood will also request your W-9 if there are any direct billing components (e.g., SOW or reserved capacity billed by Redwood). If everything is marketplace-managed, the buyer may still need to provide tax info to AWS.

- EU VAT / Reverse charge: If GreenWave is EU-registered and provides a VAT number, AWS's standard mechanism applies (reverse charge). We'll coordinate with you to ensure our invoices (if any) include correct VAT treatment.

- Brazil / Withholding: Brazil can be trickier — AWS generally issues the customer invoice; however, some Brazilian customers need withholding (IRRF) applied when paying a foreign supplier. In those cases, we typically provide the documentation required to support reduced withholding or a pass-through invoice flow when allowed.

Next steps: Vanessa, can you confirm whether this will be a public marketplace purchase or a private offer? Rishi/Marissa — I’ve looped you for tax/finance detail. Clara — if you can share the buyer's country and confirm whether you will accept a Marketplace listing purchase, we can provide the exact list of forms to upload.

Thanks,
Dylan Brooks

Hi all,

Quick clarification from the Marketplace side:
- For public listings, AWS invoices the customer and remits the net to the seller after Marketplace fees. The buyer receives an AWS invoice that includes the gross charge and any applicable taxes.
- For private offers where the seller elects to bill the customer directly, the seller issues invoices.
- W-9 vs W-8: AWS requires tax residency documentation from sellers and may request buyer docs for certain tax treatments. We recommend buyers complete forms in the AWS Billing console.

On split or pass-through invoicing: AWS supports a few flows, but the default is single-point billing by AWS. If GreenWave requires a split invoice for tax or procurement reasons, please flag that ASAP so we can evaluate a private offer or custom arrangement.

Happy to jump on a 30-minute call to map the flow for this account.

Best,
Marcus Lee
AWS Marketplace, Account Manager

Folks — adding a few technical notes for finance and for GreenWave so expectations are clear:

- W-9/W-8: If GreenWave is a US entity, a W-9 will suffice. Non-US entities should provide the appropriate W-8 series. If AWS is billing, AWS will normally rely on the buyer's AWS billing profile; but Redwood should collect a copy of the buyer's W-9/W-8 if we are performing any direct billing (SOW, reserved capacity).

- EU VAT (OSS / Reverse Charge): For SaaS delivered from outside the EU, most EU customers apply the reverse charge if they provide a valid VAT ID. AWS invoices will show tax treatment; if Redwood issues an invoice, include the buyer VAT ID and reference the reverse charge.

- Brazil (withholding and local taxes): Brazilian payers may require IRRF withholding on payments to non-resident companies. Two practical notes: 1) If AWS invoices the customer, the withholding obligation rests with the payer (GreenWave) — we can provide certificate of non-residence if requested. 2) If Redwood invoices directly, GreenWave may deduct withholding and issue an IRRF tax receipt. Either flow requires early coordination — buyer procurement often requests a signed tax declaration or local counsel confirmation.

- Recommended playbook steps (short):
  1) Confirm public vs private offer (affects who invoices).
  2) Ask buyer to upload W-9/W-8 into AWS billing (if marketplace purchase).
  3) If buyer is Brazil-based or EU with special VAT needs, surface this to AWS AMM and Redwood finance to determine pass-through / private offer needs.

I attached a quick tax-summary-table that maps by country the likely treatment (not legal advice). Happy to coordinate with PwC Brazil if GreenWave wants local confirmation.

-Rishi
Head of Finance Operations, Redwood Inference

Hi Clara — short answer: yes, a private offer is the cleanest path for split invoicing. Practical checklist for GreenWave / Redwood to enable that flow:

1) GreenWave confirms they will accept a private offer (email confirmation is fine).
2) GreenWave provides W-9 (you've attached it — thanks).
3) Redwood and AWS agree on offer terms in the AWS private offers portal (we'll propose unit pricing and which entity bills which line item).
4) Procurement/legal: execute a minimal SOW / ordering document between Redwood and GreenWave if Redwood will bill directly for reserved capacity or services.

If GreenWave prefers to proceed on the public listing and cannot accept private offers, finance will need to map AWS invoice lines into your ledger — we can provide a summarized invoice template for your AP team.

Action items:
- Dylan / Vanessa: book a 30-minute call with GreenWave + AWS to finalize public vs private decision.
- Rishi: prepare a sample private-offer invoice template and a short note on Brazilian withholding implications if we encounter Brazil-based buyers in future.
- Clara: confirm private offer acceptance or, if preferring public listing, confirm AP contact and GL mapping needs.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Revenue Ops, Redwood Inference
